question: Explain why the speed of a charged particle remains constant when it moves in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity, although its direction of motion changes continuously.

options.A: The magnetic force $\vec F=q(\vec v\times\vec B)$ is perpendicular to velocity and instantaneous displacement. Therefore $W=0$, so kinetic energy and speed remain constant; the perpendicular force continuously changes only the direction, producing circular motion.
options.B: The magnetic force is parallel to velocity, so it increases kinetic energy while turning the particle.
options.C: The magnetic field cancels the particle’s inertia, keeping its speed constant.
options.D: The magnetic force does positive work equal to the change in kinetic energy.
